* UPDATED, 2019-01-15: After careful review, the original data product algorithm (pco2_pco2wat) for this sensor was found to contain an error that resulted in calculation of incorrect derived L1 pCO2 values. In consultation with the vendor, the algorithm has been corrected, verified, and uploaded to the OOI system. This update, effective 2019-01-10, applies to all deployments for this sensor. All derived L1 pCO2 data products generated prior to this date should be re-requested in order to ensure utilization of the correct algorithm.  The updated algorithm can be viewed at  https://github.com/oceanobservatories/ion-functions/blob/master/ion_functions/data/co2_functions.py. *

Until further notice, derived L1 pCO2 data products from this sensor are incorrect and should not be used. A significant discrepancy has been uncovered between the pCO2 values from shipboard water samples vs. values calculated by OOI system. The pco2_pco2wat algorithm is under review and can be viewed at https://github.com/ooici/ion-functions/blob/master/ion_functions/data/co2_functions.py. To receive instant notification of updates to the code, add yourself as a watcher to the GitHub repository linked above. For further questions please email help@oceanobservatories.org.

Due to errors during vendor calibration, there were issues with the onboard-calculated O2 products during this deployment. The calibration files have been corrected, and the O2 values derived using the external OOI Stern-Volmer-Uchida algorithm [DO from Phase (L1 product) and DO from Phase - Corrected (L2 product)] should be considered valid. The onboard-calculated Stern-Volmer values [DO from Onboard Calculation (L1) and DO from Onboard Calculation - Corrected (L2)] should NOT be used during this time range.

Analog output from the optodes is produced by using a digital to analog converter (DAC). DAC configuration was initially only done at power up or reset, but firmware version 4.6.4 began updating configuration each time the analog output value was updated to ensure long-term continuous operation. Unfortunately, this also produced a voltage jump, creating erratic noise in the output data. The firmware has been corrected, but only the onboard-calculated Stern-Volmer values [DO from Onboard Calculation (L1 product; 'ctd_tc_oxygen') and DO from Onboard Calculation - Corrected (L2 product; 'dissolved_oxygen')] should be used during this annotated time range, NOT the 'DO from Phase' data which contain the noisy analog signal.

This resulted in the automatic protective shutdown of the primary power source for the Regional Cabled Array, which meant the system was not collecting data.

On 17 August 2020, at ~1824 hours PDT, the south cable line went offline due to an over-current event. Submarine cable repair operations commenced August 2021 utilizing an industry cable repair/installation ship, with support from the R/V Thompson and ROV Jason. The faulty Primary Node PN1B was recovered, removed from the system, and jointing activities of the replacement PN1B were completed on 15 August. The final bight was successfully deployed to the seafloor on 23 August 2021. The RCA south cable line has been powered and PN1A, PN1C, and PN1D are now fully operational.

At 06:37 PDT, power to the observatory went down due to a pump failure in Chiller #1. Chiller #2 did pick up the load, but not in time for power to automatically shut down to prevent the system from overheating.
The observatory was taken offline for a planned outage at 08:00PDT 2021-11-01 in order to perform a series of DAS experiments using the fiber optic cables and for system maintenance.

Conductivity values following the shutdown for the DAS experiment were anomalously low. A ground fault was detected on this unit just after deployment, but investigation regarding the ultimate cause is ongoing. Any parameters that rely on conductivity (salinity, density, etc.) should be used with caution.

The south line was powered down temporarily as part of the successful PN01B redeployment.

The data from this pCO2 sensor were abnormally low and exhibited a pattern of persistent spikes and fall-offs after the primary node PN01B redeployment. It's possible there was a pump malfunction or other technical issue with the instrument following power restoration. Use these data with caution.

Immediately following deployment of the BEP, the pCO2 values spiked and then slowly declined towards normal values. Investigation is ongoing, but data from this early deployment time period should be used with caution.

After a pump failure in one of the shore station chillers and a successful failover switch, a secondary chiller went offline during repairs and brought down power to the array. The pump has been replaced and both chillers are back online.
Port found in an alarm state - cleared by disabling and re-enabling the port.

The OPTAAC104 port was in an error mode again and required a restart. It is likely that communications issues will continue to occur, so the channel will be monitored. Investigation regarding the cause is ongoing.
The OPTAAC104 port continues to experience communications issues that interrupt data delivery. The channel is being monitored and investigation regarding the cause is ongoing.

Shore Station PFEs failed during chiller repair work, bringing down the north and south lines of the array. PFEs and secondary infrastructure were brought back online following chiller part replacement and repairs.
OPTAAC104 has been taken offline after repeated port errors and inability to keep the port active.

A 24h drop in conductivity followed by a return to previous values indicates a potential clog in the conductivity cell that then cleared on its own. Conductivity (and all conductivity-derived data) during this time range is suspect.

A utility power outage at the shore station and subsequent delayed transition to generator caused the PFEs to shut down. Power was restored, secondary infrastructure restarted, and instrument logging resumed on 20 June.
An issue with the chillers at the shore station resulted in a system shutdown. The system was brought back online following repairs and testing.
When deployed, the BEP ADCP was configured to collect data over 60 bins rather than the usual 81 bins.
BEP power was turned off due to an overcurrent event during Deep Profiler power on following the 2023 mooring turn. The DP extension cable was swapped and power was then restored to the node.

Power to both RCA cable segments was unexpectedly lost on 26 November due to a faulty card in the high voltage power supply. All deployed infrastructure was offline until the card and controller computer motherboard could be replaced.

We observed an unusually sudden and persistent drop in conductivity values that lasted from December to April. This could be related to several high ground fault warnings, or the conductivity cell may have been clogged with sediment. Any parameters that rely on conductivity (salinity, density, etc.) should be used with caution during this time period.

Power feed equipment at the shore station unexpectedly powered down due to an interruption in flow from the chillers during pump replacement and testing of a purge valve. Installation and maintenance of the chillers was completed later in the morning, the system was powered on in the afternoon, all tests successfully passed, and primary and secondary nodes, platforms, and instruments were then powered back up.
Rayfin scripts for CAMDS operations were found to have stopped. Scripts were restarted and image collection resumed.
Added 1 second wait between each 'TakeStill' command (instead of commands sent consecutively with no delay), and extended the wait after the 3rd 'TakeStill' from 1.5 to 3 s.

Equipment at the shore station unexpectedly powered down due to a chiller failure and incomplete failover to secondary unit. Repairs were completed later in the day, the system was powered on for testing, and then primary and secondary nodes, platforms, and instruments were brought back up.
North and south lines powered down for DAS experiment, chiller pump replacement, and network switch replacement at shore station.
A temporary distortion of the Earth’s magnetic field following a severe solar storm created compass data fluctuations between 10-12 May 2024.
A problem occurred during a routine switch from chiller #1 to #2 that resulted in power dropping to both lines.

Shore Station Chiller #2 did not successfully transfer back to chiller #1 following a fault alarm, causing a low flow alarm. This triggered a shutdown of the PFE.
Camera throws CAMERA_3 error when collecting images. Reboots required to eliminate errors.

Following a chiller changeover after a regular maintenance check, a low flow to High Voltage Power Supply (HVPS) Nos. 1 and 2 caused the system to power down. Wiring was inspected by vendor, a 5-second delay scenario was removed, and all deployed primary and secondary infrastructure are now back online.
Rebooted and remounted storage multiple times to clear errors and connect to data storage.

On Dec 11 at 0636 PT, shore station Chiller No. 2 pump failure caused the system to power down. Maintenance vendor testing could not identify an issue and the failure was not able to be recreated. Power feed equipment was energized and the North and South cables re-powered, followed by the deployed infrastructure.
PCO2W on LJ01C port faulted during power up following cable downtime. Error cleared after disable/enable cycle.

A lightning strike close to the shore station resulted in the opening of the HV breakers feeding the cables. The PFE was secured and visual inspections performed to ensure there was no equipment damage. System lightning protection performed as expected and power was restored and instruments started back up within 10 hours.
